clips.caption:
Ask how your score is calculated and the answer is: it's a secret.

Equifax, TransUnion, TRW. Three companies produce the number that decides what interest rate you get on a mortgage, a car loan, a personal loan, a home equity loan.

So it matters enormously. And the method behind it is not published.

Because the banks do not want your score to go up. The lower it is, the more interest they are allowed to charge you.

And no politician is shouting about it, because the banks are paying them.

Do you actually know your number?

clips.caption:
Five pieces of credit. He names all five and how to use them.

Two installment loans: a mortgage and a car payment. Kevin Trudeau says he carries both on purpose, for the rating. They show stability, and stability is points.

Three revolving lines: a Visa, a MasterCard, and a store card. He uses Neiman Marcus.

Then the part almost nobody gets right. Use those cards — up to about 80% of the limit at least once. That dents the score for that month, but it proves you can carry real credit.

Then pay it off. And going forward keep paying it off BEFORE the reporting date, not before the due date. Those are different days, and only one of them is the one being measured.

Stay current on the fixed loans, always.

Which of the five are you missing?

clips.caption:
A coffee can with a label on it. That was the whole system.

Kevin Trudeau grew up with a clothes line in the backyard. Everyone else in the neighbourhood had a dryer. His family did not.

In the kitchen sat an empty Maxwell House can with a strip of tape on it: DRYER FUND. Every night his father emptied his pockets into it.

He asked his parents how all those other families had dryers already. They bought it on credit, on terms. They pay for it over time and they pay interest.

Why don't we do that?

The rule in that house was one line long. If you cannot pay for something in cash, you cannot afford it. It might take a few months. It might take a year. But then you own it, and you do not pay double.

Because with the interest, that is exactly what you pay. Double.

Did your family run on cash or on credit?

#kevintrudeau #debtfree #payincash #moneylessons #financialfreedom #interest

Every book on affirmations tells you to start with "I am a millionaire." Kevin Trudeau says that's exactly wrong.

You don't start there. You end there.

Are your five closest friends opening doors for you, or closing them?

clips.caption:
There's an old line that separates winners from everyone else: losers talk about people, winners talk about events.

Kevin Trudeau's guest says he'll cut off a phone call the second it turns into gossip about someone's coworker drama, even on a Sunday morning when he technically has the time.

His reasoning is blunt: his life is short, and there are only so many years to spend on payroll, marketing and growth, let alone somebody else's argument.

It's not that winners are above other people. They just have bigger fish to fry.

Where does your own conversation go when nobody's watching — people, or events?

clips.caption:
A self-made investor turns down 99 out of every 100 pitches he hears.

Before he writes a check, he asks four questions: Is this person ride-or-die? Does anyone actually buy this product? Will it sell without you standing there explaining it? And can your team back up every claim you just made?

Kevin Trudeau's guest tells founders who claim a retail deal isn't signed yet: that's not a purchase order, that's a hope.

Most people pitch a dream. He's checking for proof.

Which of these four would your own idea actually pass right now?

clips.caption:
A guy built a $200 million business from nothing, flipping pizzas while living in his mother-in-law's basement.

The business exploded — hundreds of employees, a huge new building, more locations every year. Kevin Trudeau's guest, tax attorney Mark Kohler, told him to pull some money out. He never did.

Every dollar went straight back into the company. When the market finally turned, the overhead was too high to survive it, and he walked away penniless.

Farmers call this "land rich, cash poor" — buying more land instead of ever banking a cushion.

It isn't about how big your business gets. It's whether you ever take anything off the table.

#kevintrudeau #smallbusiness #entrepreneur #wealthmindset #businessowner #taxstrategy

Working for other law firms, he never thought twice about the cost of paperclips or the copy machine — that was someone else's problem. The day he was about to buy new equipment for his own firm, it hit him: save a thousand dollars here, and he'd effectively made a thousand dollars this month.

Cutting a tax bill by a dollar is identical to earning that dollar, without doing any extra work to get it.

Where in your own business are you still spending like it's not your money?

Most people think they need an LLC before they can write anything off. Tax attorney Mark Kohler says that's flat wrong.

He tells Kevin Trudeau you don't need any entity to deduct your auto, your marketing costs or your team — you can do all of it as a sole proprietor, using nothing but your own name. Even a simple drive to a client meeting makes the gas and the meal deductible.

Forming an LLC or corporation is about how you structure a business you already have. It has nothing to do with whether you're allowed to save on taxes.

Have you been putting off a side hustle because you thought you needed paperwork first?

clips.caption:
Here's a common error Kevin Trudeau sees people make: writing everything they have to do onto one single to-do list for tomorrow.

You can't get it all done, so most of it just sits there making you feel like you failed.

His fix: before you write anything down, ask if it actually has to happen today. If it doesn't, flip ahead in your calendar to a day when it can, and write it there instead. Nothing goes on tomorrow's list unless tomorrow is genuinely when it belongs.

A daily list only works if it's actually daily - a handful of things, not everything.

How many things on your list today don't actually belong there?

#kevintrudeau #productivity #successhabits #businesstips #timemanagement #mindset

clips.caption:
Kevin Trudeau's real risk test has nothing to do with the upside.

Most people ask what can I make first. He asks what's the actual worst case first - and forces total honesty about it. Not just I lose $100,000. The real worst case might be losing the money and getting sued on top of it.

Then: can I actually handle that, financially and emotionally? Only after answering yes does he even look at the upside. Skip that order and a $10 million upside next to a $1 million downside gets you greedy - thinking about the ten, not the mortgage on the house you'd lose.

If the worst case costs you your house, it's not the right deal for you.
